## ✨ Added

- **Sign in through a sign-in service.** Under Settings > Security > Sign-in services you can add Pocket ID, authentik, Authelia, Keycloak, Kanidm, Zitadel or any other OpenID Connect service. Enter its address, client ID and secret, run the test sign-in, and the sign-in page gets a button for it.
- **What an account set up leaves with it.** When you block or remove an account that came in through a sign-in service, the MCP clients it set up stop working, and the phones and browsers it let into your group leave it.
- **A new phrase when an account goes.** When you block or remove an account, end all of its sign-ins, or give it a lower role, KnightLoader gives your group a new phrase by itself. Your other instances, phones and browsers move to it and stay connected, and the old words that account could see let nobody new in. In a fortress, the fortress phrase changes the same way.
- **Sessions you can see.** The Sessions card lists every browser that is signed in, and you can sign any of them out, or all the others at once.
- **The password check on changes.** Before a new passkey, token, pairing or fortress change, and before a phrase shows, KnightLoader asks for your password in a small window when you signed in more than ten minutes ago. You can turn the question off.
- **KnightLoader joins a fortress.** Enter the fortress's twelve words on the Pairing page, and KnightLoader joins your other apps there. The instances, phones and browser extensions it is paired with come along, and one that was away follows once it is back.
- **Devices that did not come along are named.** The old pairing stays open until everyone has followed, for 30 days at most. A device still missing after that shows up on the Pairing page by name, so you can bring it in with the fortress phrase or remove it.
- **KnightLoader shows up with its own logo** in your other apps, and they find it on its server whatever name you give it there.
- **Open your other apps from anywhere.** Open on an app's card on the Pairing page shows that app in a new tab, behind its own password. At home the pages come straight from it, on the road through the relay, and not a single port has to be forwarded. Each app has its own switch for it. A plugin shows how it is doing instead, and the app you opened writes each visit to its log.
- **Every permission between apps has its own switch.** The Pairing page shows what the other apps of your fortress may do at KnightLoader and what KnightLoader may do at them, each with a switch of its own.
- **You can show and change the fortress phrase, or leave the fortress.** The words appear once you enter your password. A new phrase reaches every app and instance in reach, and any it missed are named, so you know where to type the new words.
- **A phrase change KnightLoader missed asks for the new words.** If every app it still reaches has moved on and none can hand the new phrase over, the Pairing page says so. Enter the new words there and KnightLoader stays the member it was. An app that never said what it is shows up under its device's name, and after a change every app still on the old phrase is named with the device it runs on.
- **You can take an app out of the fortress.** Remove on its card on the Pairing page asks first. After that the fortress lets no new app join until you change the phrase, so it offers a new phrase right away. Until then, a short line names who is out, and an app that tries to join is told why.
- **An ArrowLoop job can follow a download.** Pick a job per category under After download, and KnightLoader starts it once a package has landed and left the working folder. You can also set up a new ArrowLoop job for the category's folder right there.
- **A backup app in your fortress can keep your settings.** It fetches KnightLoader's backup and can hand it back later, and KnightLoader puts it in place at the next start, just like a restore you upload.
- **Status for dashboards.** Homepage, Homarr and the like read how KnightLoader is doing and what happened at `/api/fortress/v1/status` and `/api/fortress/v1/log`, with an API token that has the status right. That token opens nothing else.
- **More kinds of event targets.** Add target on the Automation page offers Slack, Gotify, ntfy, Matrix, e-mail and Apprise next to Discord and your own webhook. Your targets come over as they are.

## ✨ Changed

- **The sign-in is the one your whole fortress shares.** The sign-in page and the Security tile come from GlimStone 4.9.1: at most two buttons, Forgot password? as a link below them, and your browser offers a saved passkey right in the password field. Your password, two-factor authentication, recovery codes, passkeys and API tokens move along, and a browser that was signed in stays signed in. Nothing has to be set up again.
- **A password is fully optional, in the desktop app too.** Without one, KnightLoader answers on every name it is reached under, and backups download as well. A password you set in the desktop app before stays. Any length works: below 12 characters the field says the password is quick to guess and sets it all the same.
- **API tokens have one level each.** Status only, read, add and read, or everything. Your tokens keep exactly the rights they had.
- **Staying signed in.** A sign-in lasts 30 days, or 7 without a visit.
- **No network address on any page.** KnightLoader shows no address of an instance any more. Every member reads Connected or Not reachable, in the web interface, on the phone and in the browser extension.
- **Pairing runs on the code your whole fortress shares.** The twelve words, the device keys, the relay, the search on your network and the list of who is in your group come from ParleyPort's kit, which the other apps of your fortress use as well. Your group, its phones and browsers and every approval come along with the update, and instances that are not updated yet still talk to it, so you can update them one at a time.
- **Answers over the relay may be up to 8 MiB again,** so a long download list still reaches your phone away from home. This needs a ParleyPort relay with 16 MiB frames, so the project relay is updated before this release goes out. If you run your own ParleyPort, update it first too, since an older one closes the connection when an answer is that large.

- **The Android app's Play button plays through your group.** VLC or any other player opens the file without an address of the instance: the app hands the player a link on the phone itself and fetches what the player reads through the group, in pieces, so seeking works too. At home it comes straight from the instance, and away through the relay. A phone paired before this release streams at home once you scan the phrase again, and the app offers that once.

## 🗑️ Removed

- **`-reset-2fa` is gone.** Forgot password? on the sign-in page writes a code to the log, and the reset that takes it sets a new password and turns two-factor authentication off.
- **Instances are no longer added by their address.** Every app pairs the same simple way, with the twelve words. Instances you had added by address are gone after the update, the Instances page names them once, and the tokens kept for them are revoked. Enter your group's phrase on them, and they are back.
- **The Android app keeps only the connections made with the phrase.** A connection an older build saved by its address leaves the list on the first start after the update, and the app names it once. Scan your group's phrase, and it is back.
- **A relay key typed in by hand no longer pairs instances.** Older releases let you pair instances with a relay key instead of the twelve words. The relay could read along with such a key, so it is gone. An instance paired that way stands on its own after the update, and Settings > Pairing tells you so. Generate a phrase on one instance, enter it on the others, and they are back together.
- **The `knightloader-relay` image hands over to ParleyPort.** If you run your own relay with it, switch the image to `junkerderprovinz/parleyport`. ParleyPort reads the same `KL_RELAY_…` settings, so your configuration carries over as it is, and it brings the 16 MiB frames this release needs. Only the certificate folder moves to `/var/lib/parleyport/certs`, so mount your volume there or let ParleyPort fetch a new certificate.

## 🌐 Translations

- The sign-in page and the Security tile speak all 42 languages.
